ox.content.categories.accessories.faq_1_: For a whey scoop with 300 ml of water, 600 ml is enough. For a mass gainer serving you need 800 ml or more, because the serving is large and takes more liquid. An 820 ml shaker suits both and still leaves room to shake. The capacity is written into every product name.
Which shaker capacity should I choose?
ox.content.categories.accessories.faq_2_: Wash it straight after use rather than at the end of the day; the smell comes from milk or whey residue left for hours in the heat. For a smell that has set in, soak it overnight in warm water with a spoon of baking soda, then wash it. Leave the lid open so it dries.
How do I get rid of the protein smell in a shaker?
ox.content.categories.accessories.faq_3_: Yes. It goes into the same shipment as the supplements and arrives with them, and it adds no shipping charge. If your order is above {{threshold}} riyals, shipping is free for the whole order. You can also collect it with your order from the Al Khalidiyah branch in Madinah.
Does the shaker ship with the rest of the order?
ox.content.categories.accessories.intro: Accessories are the tools that make using supplements easier. The range starts today with the shaker, and a travel pill case and a spare measuring scoop will be added later. A good shaker carries a mixing ball that stops clumping, does not leak when tipped, survives the dishwasher, and does not hold the smell of whey after washing. We state the capacity in millilitres in every shaker name, because a mass gainer scoop needs more room than a whey scoop. These go into the same order and ship with it from Madinah at no extra shipping charge.
ox.content.categories.accessories.title: Shakers and Gym Accessories | OptimalX
ox.content.categories.amino_acids.faq_1_: BCAA is three branched chain amino acids: leucine, isoleucine and valine. EAA covers all nine essential amino acids including those three, so it is the broader one. Anyone getting enough protein from food and supplement may not need either.
What is the difference between BCAA and EAA?
ox.content.categories.amino_acids.faq_2_: Glutamine is an amino acid abundant in muscle, and some people who train use it to support recovery after intense sessions. The common dose on labels is 5 grams after training or before bed, and it dissolves tastelessly in water or with whey. It is not one of the basics for a beginner.
What does glutamine do for athletes?
ox.content.categories.amino_acids.faq_3_: Usually not. Whey protein already contains a good amount of branched chain amino acids in every scoop, so anyone drinking their daily serving covers that side. A BCAA drink remains an option for anyone training on an empty stomach or wanting a light flavoured drink through a long session.
Do I need BCAA if I drink whey protein?
ox.content.categories.amino_acids.intro: Amino acids are the building blocks protein is made of, sold here as a drink or as tablets. BCAA is three branched chain acids; EAA covers all nine essential acids. You will also find glutamine for after training, and arginine and citrulline for before it. Anyone getting enough protein from food and whey may not need any of them, which is why we say so in every description. The flavoured drink works as an alternative to sweetened drinks during a session.
ox.content.categories.amino_acids.title: BCAA and EAA Amino Acids | OptimalX
ox.content.categories.casein.faq_1_a: Yes. Casein is a common choice before bed because it absorbs slowly and feeds the muscles for hours during sleep. Whey absorbs faster and suits the post training window better. Both count towards your daily protein requirement, so do not add a serving beyond what you need just because it is evening.
ox.content.categories.casein.faq_1_q: Can I drink protein before bed?
ox.content.categories.casein.faq_2_a: The source is the same, milk, and the difference is in absorption speed. Whey absorbs within an hour or two, casein across five to seven hours. That is why whey sits after training and casein before bed. Anyone buying only one starts with whey because it is more flexible in use.
ox.content.categories.casein.faq_2_q: What is the difference between casein and whey?
ox.content.categories.casein.faq_3_a: Casein takes up more water than whey, so use 250 to 300 ml of water or milk per scoop and shake it with the mixing ball. Anyone who wants it thick uses less liquid and gets a pudding like texture eaten with a spoon. Heating it is not recommended.
ox.content.categories.casein.faq_3_q: How do I mix casein so it does not clump?
ox.content.categories.casein.intro: Casein is the second protein in milk alongside whey, and it differs in how fast it absorbs. It forms a gel in the stomach and releases amino acids slowly over several hours, which is why it is taken before bed or across long gaps between meals. Its texture is thicker than whey and it works as a pudding or a thick shake with a little water. One serving gives about 24 grams of protein. It is not a replacement for whey after training, but a complement to it at a different time of day.
ox.content.categories.casein.title: Casein Protein, Slow Release | OptimalX
ox.content.categories.collagen_beauty.fa: Daily, at 10 to 20 grams dissolved in water, coffee or any drink, hot or cold, at any time. Typical use runs for eight to twelve weeks before judging any difference. What you notice varies from person to person, and nobody promises it.

The source only. Bovine is extracted from cattle hide, marine from fish skin and scales. Both are hydrolysed peptides that dissolve in drinks at the same dose. Anyone avoiding bovine products or preferring a marine source picks marine; otherwise the use is much the same and the difference is in price.
What is the difference between bovine and marine collagen?

Biotin is a B group vitamin that contributes to the maintenance of normal hair and skin. That is nutrition level wording, not a promise of a result. Common doses in supplements are 3000 to 10000 micrograms a day, and being water soluble it can be taken at any time, with or without food.
ox.content.categories.collagen_beauty.in: Collagen peptides are a hydrolysed protein powder from cattle or fish skin, with little taste, dissolving in coffee or water, hot or cold. It is taken daily at 10 to 20 grams, and typical use runs for weeks before judging any difference. Here you will find bovine and marine collagen, collagen blends with vitamin C and biotin in tablets, and biotin on its own. All of them are taken by mouth and contribute to the maintenance of normal hair and skin at the nutrition level; they are not products applied to the skin.
ox.content.categories.collagen_beauty.ti: Collagen Peptides, Marine and Bovine | OptimalX
ox.content.categories.creatine.faq_1_a: There is no decisive difference between the two. What matters is consistency at a fixed daily dose, on training days and rest days alike. Anyone who prefers a set time takes it after training with a meal that contains carbohydrates. Read the full creatine guide if you are starting for the first time.
ox.content.categories.creatine.faq_1_q: When do I take creatine, before or after training?
ox.content.categories.creatine.faq_2_a: The common dose for creatine monohydrate is 3 to 5 grams a day, which is one scoop in most packs. Check the scoop weight on the label because it differs between brands; we write it in the first line of the description. A loading phase at a larger dose is optional, not a requirement.
ox.content.categories.creatine.faq_2_q: How many scoops of creatine a day?
ox.content.categories.creatine.faq_3_a: Micronised is the same creatine monohydrate with finer particles, so it dissolves in water more easily and does not settle at the bottom of the cup. The active substance and the dose are the same in both. The price difference is small, and if plain monohydrate dissolves well for you there is no need to change.
ox.content.categories.creatine.faq_3_q: What is the difference between creatine monohydrate and micronised?
ox.content.categories.creatine.intro: Creatine monohydrate is a compound found naturally in meat and stored by the muscles, and it supports energy production in short high intensity efforts such as lifting and sprinting. The form shown here is monohydrate alone because it is the simplest and the least expensive, as a powder or micronised so it dissolves easily. The dose printed on labels is 3 to 5 grams a day, on training days and rest days. We do not sell a creatine made for cutting or a creatine for women, because there is no such thing: the substance is one and the dose is one.
ox.content.categories.creatine.title: Creatine Monohydrate in Saudi Arabia | OptimalX
ox.content.categories.daily_health.faq_1: After a long, sweaty session, on a hot day outdoors, or on a trip. One tablet dissolves in about 500 ml of water and replaces the sodium, potassium and magnesium lost in sweat. On an ordinary day with a short workout, water alone is enough and the tablet is not needed.
When do I use electrolyte tablets?
ox.content.categories.daily_health.faq_2: Look at three numbers on the pack: the number of strains, the colony forming units such as 25 billion, and whether it is stored in the fridge or outside it. It is usually taken as one capsule a day, with or before food. Weeks of consistency is the norm, and we write those three numbers into every product description.
How do I choose a probiotic?
ox.content.categories.daily_health.faq_3: A green plant extract added a spoon or two at a time to a glass of water and drunk once a day. The flavoured version tastes lightly of mint. Many people use it as part of a morning water routine. We claim no specific effect for it: the label describes it as a food supplement, and that is what we hold to.
What is liquid chlorophyll and how is it used?
ox.content.categories.daily_health.intro: Daily health is the group of products that belong to a routine rather than to training: probiotics as a daily capsule, concentrated greens and liquid chlorophyll added to water, and effervescent electrolyte tablets for hot, sweaty days. None of them is tied to a session time, and you do not have to be training to use them. Read the number of strains on the probiotic pack, and the sodium and potassium on the electrolyte pack: those are the two numbers that separate one product from another, and we write them into the description.
ox.content.categories.daily_health.title: Daily Health: Probiotics and Electrolytes | OptimalX
ox.content.categories.mass_gainer.faq_1_: A mass gainer contributes to weight gain when it adds calories above your daily requirement, because it brings carbohydrates and protein together in one high calorie serving. What happens to your weight follows your total food and training and varies from person to person. We state no number, because the number belongs to you, not to the product.
Does a mass gainer add weight?
ox.content.categories.mass_gainer.faq_2_: The usual amount is one serving a day. Some products count a serving as two large scoops and some as three, and the number is in the first line of the description. The serving can be split in two if it sits heavy, or you can start with half a serving in the first days.
How many scoops of mass gainer a day?
ox.content.categories.mass_gainer.faq_3_: Some mass gainers add creatine to the formula and some do not, and where it is present the amount is usually below the normal daily dose. Check the ingredient panel on the pack before adding a separate creatine; we note its presence in the product description.
Does a mass gainer contain creatine?
ox.content.categories.mass_gainer.intro: A mass gainer is a powder that brings carbohydrates and protein together in one high calorie serving, for anyone who finds it hard to reach their daily calories from food alone. One serving can give 600 to 1250 calories and 50 grams of protein, and its scoop is far bigger than a whey scoop. It is taken between meals or after training, not instead of meals. We do not state how much it adds to your weight here, because that follows your total food and training and varies from person to person.
ox.content.categories.mass_gainer.title: Mass Gainer and Weight Gain Protein | OptimalX
ox.content.categories.omega_3.faq_1_a: With a meal that contains fat to improve absorption, at any time of day. Many people take it with lunch or dinner. Anyone who tastes fish after the capsule keeps the pack in the fridge or takes it with the larger meal. Daily consistency matters more than the time.
ox.content.categories.omega_3.faq_2_a: They are the two active fatty acids in fish oil, and the number beside them is what you actually get per serving. A capsule carrying 1000 mg of fish oil may give only 300 mg of the two in less concentrated products, with the rest being other oils. Compare that number between products, not the capsule size.
ox.content.categories.omega_3.faq_2_q: What do EPA and DHA on the pack mean?
ox.content.categories.omega_3.faq_3_a: Omega-3 on its own is the one usually missing from food; 6 and 9 come from everyday cooking oils. A 3-6-9 blend brings all three into one capsule with less omega-3 in it. Anyone buying for EPA and DHA picks concentrated fish oil; anyone who wants a general blend picks 3-6-9.
ox.content.categories.omega_3.faq_3_q: What is the difference between omega-3 and omega 3-6-9?
ox.content.categories.omega_3.intro: Omega-3 are essential fatty acids the body does not make, and their source in supplements is fish oil in softgels. The number people who know look at is not the total fish oil on the front of the pack, but the EPA and DHA per serving on the back label, and we write it into every product description. They are taken with a meal that contains fat, at any time of day. Here you will find concentrated fish oil, and an omega 3-6-9 blend for anyone who wants all three in one capsule.
ox.content.categories.omega_3.title: Omega-3 Fish Oil | OptimalX
ox.content.categories.plant_protein.faq_: Yes, when enough of it is taken within a diet that covers your daily requirement. A blend that combines more than one source, such as pea and rice, is preferable so the essential amino acids are complete. The difference between it and whey in a single serving is small once the protein amount is equal.
Does plant protein contribute to building muscle?

It is free of milk by nature, which is why many people choose it. Gluten depends on the product and the manufacturer: some packs carry a gluten free statement and some do not. We write the protein source and the allergens stated on the label into every product description, so read them before buying.
Is plant protein free of milk and gluten?

Because pea and rice carry a mild earthy taste and a thicker texture than milk whey. Brands cover it with cocoa or vanilla and by milling the powder finer. Try it with plant milk or in a smoothie rather than water alone, and start with a small pack until you find the flavour that suits you.
Why does plant protein taste different?
ox.content.categories.plant_protein.intr: Plant protein is a protein powder from pea, rice or a blend of the two, for anyone avoiding milk or preferring a plant source. Blends that combine more than one source give a complete profile of essential amino acids, which is why we prefer them to a single source. A scoop gives 20 to 24 grams of protein, the texture is slightly thicker than whey and it needs more water. Taste varies between brands more than it does in whey, so start with the smaller pack if you are trying it for the first time.
ox.content.categories.pre_workout.faq_1_: A supplement taken about 20 to 30 minutes before training, usually containing caffeine, citrulline and beta alanine to support energy and focus during the session. It is not a requirement for anyone, and many people are fine with a cup of coffee beforehand. It helps most where you train at a time of day when you feel sluggish.
ox.content.categories.pre_workout.faq_2_: Yes. There are stimulant free versions built on citrulline and beta alanine, and they suit anyone who trains in the evening, prefers to avoid caffeine, or already drinks coffee. Look for stimulant free or stim free on the pack; we write it into the product name and into a filter of its own.
Is there a caffeine free pre-workout?
ox.content.categories.pre_workout.faq_3_: Light tingling on the skin after beta alanine is a common, temporary sensation that passes within minutes, and it does not mean the dose is wrong. Splitting the serving in two, or starting with half a serving, reduces it. If it bothers you, choose a version without beta alanine; we note its presence in every product description.
Why do I feel tingling after a pre-workout?
ox.content.categories.pre_workout.intro: A pre-workout is taken about 20 to 30 minutes before training and usually contains caffeine, citrulline and beta alanine to support energy and focus during the session. Here you will find caffeinated versions at different doses, stimulant free versions for anyone who trains in the evening, and stimulant amino acid drinks that are lighter than a full pre-workout. The most important number on the pack is the caffeine per serving, and we write it into every product description. Start with half a serving the first time, and do not combine two caffeinated products on the same day.
ox.content.categories.pre_workout.title: Pre-Workout Supplements | OptimalX
ox.content.categories.protein.faq_1_a: Whey concentrate is the lower cost base and suits most people who train. Isolate is filtered further, so its protein share is higher and its lactose lower. Casein absorbs slowly and is taken before bed. Plant protein is for anyone avoiding milk. A mass gainer is protein with carbohydrates and high calories, for anyone who needs to raise their total intake.
ox.content.categories.protein.faq_1_q: What is the difference between the types of protein powder?
ox.content.categories.protein.faq_2_a: One scoop usually gives 20 to 25 grams of protein, and one to two scoops a day is enough for most people to complete what food provides. What matters more is total protein across the day from food and supplement together. The label sets the scoop weight for each product, and we show it on the product page.
ox.content.categories.protein.faq_2_q: How many scoops of protein a day?
ox.content.categories.protein.faq_3_a: Protein powder is a food supplement sourced from milk or plants. Healthy people use it to complete their daily protein target within a balanced diet, and it does not replace meals. The amount and method of use are printed on every pack's label. For medical conditions or medication questions, see your doctor.
ox.content.categories.protein.intro: Protein powder gives 20 to 25 grams of protein per scoop and is used to complete what food provides when it is not enough. The whole family is here: whey concentrate for daily use, whey isolate for the least lactose and calories, slow absorbing casein before bed, plant protein from pea and rice, and a mass gainer for anyone who needs extra calories. Every product carries its servings, serving size and expiry date. Start with the type that suits when you use it, not with the best known brand.
ox.content.categories.protein.title: Protein Powder in Saudi Arabia | OptimalX
ox.content.categories.snacks_bars.faq_1_: In protein terms, almost: a bar gives about 20 grams, the same as a scoop. The difference is in calories, since a bar carries 200 to 230 because of the fat and fibre, while a scoop with water is about 120. The bar is the practical choice away from home; the scoop costs less on an ordinary day.
Is a protein bar a replacement for a scoop of whey?
ox.content.categories.snacks_bars.faq_2_: Protein chips are baked from milk or soy protein instead of potato, so a small bag gives about 19 grams of protein and 4 grams of carbohydrate. Ordinary chips give carbohydrate and fat with little protein to speak of. The taste is close, and the texture is lighter and crisper.
What is the difference between protein chips and ordinary chips?
ox.content.categories.snacks_bars.faq_3_: Because they are what gets mixed with whey and mass gainers most often. Quick oats go into the shaker to raise carbohydrates, and natural peanut butter adds fat and calories for anyone who needs them. We pick versions free of added sugar and hydrogenated oils, and we write the full ingredient list into the description.
Why do we sell oats and peanut butter in a supplement store?
ox.content.categories.snacks_bars.intro: Protein snacks are what you eat between meals when you want protein instead of sugar: low sugar protein bars, baked protein chips, quick oats and natural peanut butter. One bar usually gives 20 grams of protein and under 2 grams of sugar, and both numbers are in every product description alongside the calories. They are sold by the box rather than the piece, and we state the pieces per box in the first line. Store them somewhere cool, especially through a Madinah summer.
ox.content.categories.snacks_bars.title: Protein Snacks: Chips, Cookies, Oats | OptimalX
With a meal that contains fat, because it is fat soluble, at any time of day. Common daily doses in supplements are 1000 to 5000 international units. The 50000 unit dose is a weekly dose dispensed under professional guidance, and we do not sell it in the store. The version with K2 is an option for anyone who prefers both in one capsule.
When do I take vitamin D?

Magnesium is the one most used in the evening because it is gentle on the stomach, at a common dose of 200 to 400 mg. Citrate absorbs well too. The form is written on the label under the element name, and we note it in every product description. ZMA combines magnesium with zinc and vitamin B6.
Which form of magnesium suits the evening?

Yes, and combining them in one product is common. Zinc is better taken with food because it can sit heavily on an empty stomach. The common daily dose for zinc in supplements is 15 to 30 mg, and for vitamin C 500 to 1000 mg. Check your multivitamin label if you take one so the zinc is not repeated.
Can I take zinc with vitamin C?

Vitamins and minerals are the daily base that has nothing to do with a training time: multivitamins for men and for women, vitamin D3 alone or with K2, vitamin C, zinc, magnesium, and ZMA for the evening. The aim is to complete what food may be missing, not to replace it. The number that matters is the amount of each element per serving on the label, not the tablet count. Pick one or two products you can stay consistent with, and read the labels so the same element is not repeated in two products.
Vitamins and Minerals in Saudi Arabia | OptimalX
ox.content.categories.whey_isolate.faq_1: Isolate is filtered further, so its protein share is higher and its lactose and fat lower per scoop. Concentrate costs less and keeps more of the milk components. Both are complete protein sources from milk whey. Anyone who has no problem with concentrate has no need to switch.
What is the difference between isolate and concentrate?
ox.content.categories.whey_isolate.faq_2: ISO 100 is a product name from Dymatize, and it is a hydrolysed whey protein isolate. So it is a kind of whey, not a different category. It stands out for fast absorption and low lactose, and carries 25 grams of protein per scoop. You will find it here among the isolates alongside its alternatives.
What is the difference between whey protein and ISO 100?
ox.content.categories.whey_isolate.faq_3: Isolate contains a very small amount of lactose, which is why many people who find concentrate heavy prefer it. But it is derived from milk and is not considered entirely free of it. Anyone avoiding milk completely will find plant protein the better fit, and we write the protein source in every description.
Is isolate suitable for someone avoiding lactose?
ox.content.categories.whey_isolate.intro: Whey isolate is whey protein that has been filtered further, so the protein share per scoop is higher and the lactose, fat and calories are lower. It suits anyone counting calories closely, anyone who finds concentrate heavy on the stomach, and anyone who wants the least lactose. Some products here are hydrolysed, meaning broken into shorter chains for faster absorption. The difference in a single serving is small and the difference in price is clear, so choose isolate when you have a reason for it, not because it costs more.
ox.content.categories.whey_isolate.title: Whey Protein Isolate, Authentic | OptimalX
ox.content.categories.whey_protein.faq_1: Both are fine and the difference between them is small. Total protein across the day matters more than exact timing. Anyone training on an empty stomach may prefer a scoop beforehand; anyone who ate two hours before the session takes it after. On rest days the scoop counts within the normal meals of the day.
When do I take whey protein, before or after training?
ox.content.categories.whey_protein.faq_2: Whey protein on its own is low in calories: a scoop with water is about 120 calories. Weight follows your total intake across the day, not the supplement alone. It is used within weight gain goals with milk and oats, and within weight management with water only, depending on the rest of the diet.
ox.content.categories.whey_protein.faq_3: It depends on the size. A 5 pound tub, that is 2.27 kg, usually gives 60 to 75 servings, and a 2 pound tub about 28 to 30. The exact number is on the label under servings, and we put it in the first line of every product description so packs are easy to compare.
How many scoops are in a tub of whey protein?
ox.content.categories.whey_protein.intro: Whey protein comes from milk whey and is the most used type of protein powder because it absorbs quickly and carries a complete amino acid profile. What is shown here is concentrate and its blends, giving about 24 grams of protein per scoop with a small amount of lactose and fat. It is taken after training or between meals with water or milk. ox.content.glossary.bcaa.def: Three amino acids, leucine, isoleucine and valine, sold as a drink during training.
ox.content.glossary.beta_alanine.def: An amino acid in pre-workouts that causes light, temporary tingling on the skin.
ox.content.glossary.biotin.def: A B group vitamin that contributes to the maintenance of normal hair and skin.
ox.content.glossary.caffeine.def: The milligrams of caffeine in one serving, the number you add to the coffee in your day.
ox.content.glossary.calories.def: The energy in one serving, counted within your day's total rather than on top of it.
ox.content.glossary.carbohydrates.def: The grams of carbohydrate in one serving, sugars, starches and fibre included.
ox.content.glossary.casein.def: The slow absorbing milk protein, taken before bed or between widely spaced meals.
ox.content.glossary.citrulline.def: An ingredient in pre-workouts used to support endurance during a session.
ox.content.glossary.closing: Could not find the term you were looking for? Send it to us in writing and we will add it with an explanation.
ox.content.glossary.collagen.def: Hydrolysed, tasteless collagen that dissolves in drinks at 10 to 20 grams a day.
ox.content.glossary.concentrate.def: Whey with basic filtration, 70 to 80 grams of protein per 100 grams, and the least expensive form.
ox.content.glossary.creatine.def: A compound stored by the muscles that supports energy production in short high intensity effort, at 3 to 5 grams a day.
ox.content.glossary.eaa.def: The nine amino acids the body does not make, including the three branched chain ones.
ox.content.glossary.electrolytes.def: The sodium, potassium and magnesium salts lost in sweat, sold as tablets that dissolve in water.
ox.content.glossary.fat.def: The grams of fat in one serving, counted within the day's calories like protein and carbohydrate.
ox.content.glossary.fibre.def: The grams of dietary fibre in one serving, the part of the carbohydrate the body does not digest.
ox.content.glossary.glutamine.def: An amino acid abundant in muscle, used after training at a 5 gram dose.
ox.content.glossary.hydrolysed.def: Isolate whose proteins have been cut into shorter chains so it absorbs faster.
ox.content.glossary.isolate.def: Whey with extra filtration: more protein and less lactose and fat per serving.
ox.content.glossary.iu.def: A unit for the dose of some vitamins such as D3; it is not the same as a milligram.
ox.content.glossary.lactose.def: The milk sugar that is lower in isolate and almost absent in the hydrolysed form.
ox.content.glossary.loading.def: A week at a larger creatine dose to reach full stores faster; it is optional.
ox.content.glossary.magnesium.def: A form of magnesium that is gentle on the stomach, taken in the evening at 200 to 400 mg.
ox.content.glossary.mass_gainer.def: A powder that brings carbohydrates and protein together in one high calorie serving.
ox.content.glossary.micronised.def: The same creatine monohydrate with finer particles so it dissolves more easily.
ox.content.glossary.nutrition_facts.def: The panel on the pack that states calories, protein and carbohydrates per serving.
ox.content.glossary.omega_3.def: Essential fatty acids sourced from fish oil; the number that matters is the EPA and DHA per serving.
ox.content.glossary.page_title: Supplement Glossary: Whey, Isolate, Creatine | OptimalX
ox.content.glossary.plant_protein.def: Protein from pea, rice or a blend of the two, for anyone avoiding milk.
ox.content.glossary.pre_workout.def: A blend of caffeine, citrulline and beta alanine taken half an hour before a session.
ox.content.glossary.probiotic.def: Beneficial bacteria in capsules; the two numbers that matter are the strain count and the colony forming units.
ox.content.glossary.protein.def: The grams of protein in one serving, the number you compare one powder with another by.
ox.content.glossary.saturated_fat.def: The saturated part of the fat in a serving, printed on its own line under total fat.
ox.content.glossary.scoop.def: The measuring tool inside the pack; its weight differs between products, so check it on the label.
ox.content.glossary.serving.def: The amount set on the label for one use; the number of servings is what you compare packs by.
ox.content.glossary.sodium.def: The milligrams of sodium in one serving, the salt figure on the label, higher in electrolyte drinks.
ox.content.glossary.stim_free.def: A pre-workout without caffeine, for anyone training in the evening or avoiding stimulants.
ox.content.glossary.sugars.def: The grams of sugar in one serving, both the added sugar and the sugar already in the ingredients.
ox.content.glossary.vitamin_c.def: The milligrams of vitamin C in one serving, listed on the label with its share of the daily reference intake.
ox.content.glossary.vitamin_d3.def: A fat soluble vitamin taken with a meal, at a common dose of 1000 to 5000 international units.
ox.content.glossary.whey.def: A protein extracted from the liquid left after cheese making, fast absorbing and complete in amino acids.
ox.content.glossary.zinc.def: The milligrams of zinc in one serving, listed on the label with its share of the daily reference intake.
ox.content.glossary.zma.def: A blend of zinc, magnesium and vitamin B6 taken before bed.
ox.content.goals.energy.faq_1_a: About 20 to 30 minutes before training with a glass of water. It is better avoided late in the evening because caffeine can affect sleep. On rest days you do not need it. And if you drink coffee the same day, count it in your total caffeine.
ox.content.goals.energy.faq_2_a: Yes. There are stimulant free versions built on citrulline and beta alanine. They suit anyone who trains in the evening, anyone who prefers to avoid caffeine, and anyone who already drinks coffee before training. Look for "stimulant free" or "stim free" on the pack; we write it into the product name.
ox.content.goals.energy.faq_2_q: Is there a caffeine free pre-workout?

Someone who eats a varied diet every day may be fine with vitamin D3 and omega-3. And anyone who wants to know what they are actually short of gets there through testing with a qualified health provider, not guesswork.
ox.content.goals.general_health.faq_1_q: Do I need a multivitamin if my diet is balanced?
ox.content.goals.general_health.faq_2_a: With a meal that contains fat, because it is fat soluble, at any time of day. Common daily doses in supplements are 1000 to 5000 international units. ox.content.goals.general_health.faq_2_q: When do I take vitamin D3?

ox.content.goals.general_health.faq_3_q: Can I take omega-3 and vitamin D at the same time?

ox.content.goals.performance.explainer_1: Gym supplements is a general name for any product taken to complete food during a training period. Four are the most common. The first is protein, a powder from whey or from plants that gives 20 to 25 grams of protein per scoop and is used when food does not cover your daily requirement. The second is creatine monohydrate, a compound found naturally in meat that supports energy production in short high intensity work, at a fixed daily dose of 3 to 5 grams. The third is pre-workout, a blend of caffeine, citrulline and beta alanine taken half an hour before a session to support focus and energy. The fourth is amino acids such as BCAA and EAA, the building blocks of protein itself in drink form.
ox.content.goals.performance.explainer_2: A beginner does not need all four. First comes a steady training programme, enough sleep, and food that covers protein. Then whey protein if food is not enough, and creatine if you lift regularly. Pre-workout and amino acids come later, and may never come at all. A supplement closes a specific gap; it does not make up for what is missing in the basics. If you want to know which gap is yours, send us a written question and we will answer without exaggeration.
ox.content.goals.performance.explainer_t: What gym supplements are, and what a beginner needs
ox.content.goals.performance.faq_1_a: Whey protein if your food does not cover your protein requirement, and creatine monohydrate at a fixed daily dose. Those two are enough for the first months. Pre-workout and amino acids are later additions, not a condition for starting. More important than any supplement are sleep, food and consistency in training.
ox.content.goals.performance.faq_1_q: Which gym supplements matter most for a beginner?
ox.content.goals.performance.faq_2_a: No. Each supplement here plays a specific role, and many of them overlap. Anyone drinking whey protein already gets branched chain amino acids from it, so a separate BCAA is usually unnecessary. Ask us before you buy more than two products; it is cheaper than trying everything.
ox.content.goals.performance.faq_2_q: Do I need all of these supplements together?
ox.content.goals.performance.faq_3_a: Protein is a food source that contributes to the maintenance and growth of muscle mass. Creatine is a compound that supports energy production in short high intensity work. They can be used together in the same cup, and each has its own dose printed on the label.

ox.content.goals.recovery.faq_1_a: One scoop usually gives 20 to 25 grams of protein, and that is enough for most people after a session. What matters more is total protein across the day, not the single scoop. Anyone eating a full meal within an hour or two of training may not need the scoop at all.
ox.content.goals.recovery.faq_1_q: How many scoops of protein after training?
ox.content.goals.recovery.faq_2_a: Yes. Casein is a common choice before bed because it absorbs slowly and feeds the muscles for hours. Whey absorbs faster and suits the post training window better. Both count towards your daily protein requirement, so do not add a serving beyond what you need.
ox.content.goals.recovery.faq_2_q: Can I drink protein before bed?
ox.content.goals.recovery.faq_3_a: Magnesium is a mineral that contributes to normal muscle function, and part of it leaves the body with sweat. Many people who train take it in the evening as part of a bedtime routine. The common dose in supplements is 200 to 400 mg, and the glycinate form is a common choice because it is gentle on the stomach.
ox.content.goals.recovery.faq_3_q: What does magnesium do for someone who trains?
ox.content.goals.recovery.intro: Recovery supplements are what comes after the session and before sleep: fast protein after training, slow casein before bed, amino acids, magnesium and electrolytes. The idea is simple. Training stresses the muscle, rest and food rebuild it, and a supplement closes a specific gap in that routine. Enough sleep remains the part no product replaces.
